hero.name: Sanghyeon Shin
hero.lead: A service planner who finds the answer in what users actually do, then builds and ships.
hero.summary:
As a LIKELION intern, I planned and ran a community platform for 80 universities and **took a 2,000-person national hackathon from planning through the finals**. With a limited ops team, I **built automation tools myself and put them to work** where the bottlenecks were: participant inquiries, checking 562 submitted repos, and tallying the finals.

Beyond that, over two years I've built, shipped, and run 15+ services myself, from screens to backend and AI tooling, and learned that what makes a plan convincing isn't the finished screen, but **what I decided about the user and on what evidence**. Next, I want to **make the next decision from the data users leave behind, and check that decision with users again**.

principles.heading: How I work.
principles.to_projects: See how the three steps played out in the projects

items.t:
I find the problem
in what users actually do.
items.d: I start by watching how users and operators really move, and I re-check common assumptions against data. The point where people keep getting stuck becomes the problem the product has to solve.

items.t:
I turn that problem into a flow and rules,
and build it myself.
items.d: I design the user flow and the policy, and when needed I build it myself, from the screens to the backend and AI tooling, so it becomes a product that actually runs. Being able to check that it works as planned cuts the communication cost between planning and development.

items.t:
After launch, I watch users
and fix it again.
items.d: Launch is where user data starts coming in. I run the product where it's actually used and feed the questions and problems back into it.

figures.heading: Changes I can prove in numbers
figures.sub: Only what actually changed in operations.

changes.label: Participant inquiries
changes.d: The FAQ bot answered 80.8% of inquiries instantly by keyword, and the staff spent 15 minutes a day reviewing the bot log and filling in missing answers.
changes.basis: Basis: one month after the FAQ bot · 229 questions · 0 unanswered · staff time includes log review and answer updates · 14th hackathon

changes.label: Submission checks
changes.d: Post-deadline commits, force-pushes, and private flips were detected automatically across every branch, and the staff made the verdicts against criteria agreed before the scan.
changes.basis: Basis: after the 314-team deadline · 5 violations found · 14th hackathon

changes.label: Finals results reveal
changes.d: Judges' votes gathered in a console I built and reached the stage screen in 2.2 seconds.

changes.label: 13th cohort session attendance
changes.d: Staff put up a QR code, members scan it on their phones, it's recorded on the server instantly, lateness is judged automatically at the 20-minute mark, and only late or absent members show up on the roll.
changes.basis: Basis: 45 members of HUFS LIKELION's 13th cohort · WelcomeKit PWA
